indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.4.2.1 Demonstrate knowledge of generation of electricity, its transmission and transformation into other forms
indicator.objective: Identify the components of an electric circuit and their functions

skills.description: Name basic components: battery/dry cell, connecting wire, switch, bulb/LED.
State the simple function of each component (battery supplies energy, wire carries current, switch opens/closes circuit, bulb lights).
Draw a simple circuit showing battery, wire, switch and bulb.
Connect components to make a bulb/LED light (practical).
Recognise a complete circuit versus an incomplete circuit.
Identify other materials that can be used in place of dry cells, wires, or bulbs (e.g. lemon as battery, foil as wire).

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: A bulb can light without a complete circuit.
The switch is not needed in a circuit.
The battery is not part of the circuit.
A circuit can work with only one wire.
LEDs and bulbs work in exactly the same way.

questions.stem: Which of these is a basic component of an electric circuit?
hints: Which one stores energy for the circuit?
It has two ends, positive and negative.
questions.explanation: A battery is a basic component of an electric circuit. It supplies energy to make the circuit work.
questions.misconception: The battery is not part of the circuit.

questions.stem: Which set lists only basic components of an electric circuit?
hints: Which set has parts used in a real circuit?
A switch, bulb, wire and battery all belong in a circuit.
questions.explanation: The basic components of an electric circuit are the battery, bulb, connecting wire and switch.
questions.misconception: Any object can be part of an electric circuit.

questions.stem: Name two basic components of an electric circuit.
questions.explanation: Two basic components are the battery and the bulb. Other components include the switch and connecting wires.
questions.misconception: Only the bulb matters in a circuit.

questions.stem: A pupil lists four items: battery, wire, switch, bulb. Which of these is NOT a basic component of an electric circuit?
hints: Which one is not used to make a simple circuit?
A magnet is not part of a simple circuit.
questions.explanation: A magnet is not a basic component of an electric circuit. The basic components are battery, wire, switch and bulb.
questions.misconception: Any object can be used in a circuit.

questions.stem: What is the function of the battery in an electric circuit?
options: It opens and closes the circuit
questions.explanation: The battery supplies energy to the circuit. This energy makes the bulb light and the components work.
questions.misconception: The battery is not important.

questions.stem: What is the function of the switch in an electric circuit?
options: It opens and closes the circuit
hints: A switch can be on or off.
questions.explanation: The switch opens and closes the circuit. When the switch is closed, electricity flows; when open, the circuit is broken.
questions.misconception: A switch is not needed in a circuit.

questions.stem: What is the function of the connecting wire in an electric circuit?
answer: it carries electricity around the circuit
questions.explanation: The connecting wire carries electricity around the circuit, linking the battery, switch and bulb.
questions.misconception: Wires are not important in a circuit.

questions.stem: Match the component to its function. Which pair is correct?
options: Wire → opens and closes the circuit
hints: Think about what each part does.
questions.explanation: The battery supplies energy. The bulb gives light, the switch opens/closes the circuit, and the wire carries electricity.
questions.misconception: The bulb supplies energy.

questions.stem: When will a bulb in a simple circuit light up?
hints: A complete circuit lets electricity flow.
questions.explanation: A bulb lights up only when the circuit is complete, allowing electricity to flow through it.
questions.misconception: A bulb lights even if the circuit is broken.

questions.stem: What happens if the connecting wire in a circuit is cut?
questions.explanation: If the wire is cut, the circuit is broken. Electricity cannot flow, so the bulb does not light.
questions.misconception: A bulb lights even with a broken wire.

questions.stem: A pupil connects a battery, wire and bulb, but the bulb does not light. What is the most likely reason?
questions.explanation: The most likely reason is that the circuit is not complete. A loose connection or a gap in the circuit stops electricity from flowing.
questions.misconception: The bulb lights even if the circuit is broken.

questions.stem: A pupil wants to make a simple circuit but has no dry cell. Which of these can be used instead to supply energy?
hints: A lemon can act as a simple battery.
questions.explanation: A lemon can be used as a simple battery to supply energy in a circuit.
questions.misconception: Only dry cells can supply energy.

questions.stem: Name one material that can be used as a connecting wire in an emergency.
hints: It must be a metal that conducts electricity.
Think of something thin and metallic.
questions.explanation: Materials like aluminium foil, paper clips, or metal spoons can be used as connecting wires because they conduct electricity.
questions.misconception: Any material can carry electricity.

questions.stem: A pupil wants to make a simple circuit but has no switch. What can they use instead to open and close the circuit?
hints: The switch needs to conduct electricity when closed.
A metal paper clip can be bent to make or break contact.
questions.explanation: A metal paper clip can be used as a simple switch because it conducts electricity and can be moved to open or close the circuit.
questions.misconception: Any material can be used as a switch.

questions.stem: Draw a simple electric circuit with a battery, a bulb, and connecting wires.

criteria.description: Drew a battery in the circuit
Drew a bulb in the circuit
Drew connecting wires linking the components
The drawing forms a complete loop (closed circuit)

hints: Connect the bulb to the battery with wires.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: The circuit does not need to form a complete loop.

questions.stem: Draw a simple circuit that includes a battery, a switch, a bulb and connecting wires. Label all four components.

criteria.description: Drew a battery and labeled it
Drew a switch and labeled it
Drew a bulb and labeled it
Drew connecting wires and labeled them
The components form a complete closed loop

questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Some components can be left out of the drawing.

questions.stem: Draw a circuit diagram using symbols for a battery, a switch and a bulb. Show the switch in the open position and in the closed position.

criteria.description: Used correct symbols for battery, switch and bulb
Drew the switch in the open position
Drew the switch in the closed position
Both diagrams form complete loops (except at the open switch)

hints: Use simple symbols for each component.
Open switch = gap in the circuit.
questions.explanation: This is a drawing task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: Open and closed switches look the same in a diagram.

questions.stem: In groups, use a battery, connecting wires and a bulb. Connect them to make the bulb light. Show your working circuit to your teacher.

criteria.description: Connected the battery, wires and bulb correctly
Made the bulb light
Worked safely and cooperatively in the group

hints: Make sure all connections are tight.
The circuit must be complete for the bulb to light.
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: The bulb can light even if the circuit is not complete.

questions.stem: In groups, build a circuit with a battery, wire, switch and bulb. Show how the switch turns the bulb on and off.

criteria.description: Built a circuit with battery, wire, switch and bulb
Showed the bulb lighting when the switch is closed
Showed the bulb going off when the switch is open

hints: Close the switch to let electricity flow.
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: The switch is not needed in a circuit.

questions.stem: In groups, build a circuit with a battery, wire and bulb. Test different materials (e.g. a metal spoon, a plastic ruler, a piece of paper) by placing them in the circuit. Record which materials let the bulb light and which do not.

criteria.description: Built a working circuit with battery, wire and bulb
Tested at least three different materials
Correctly recorded which materials let the bulb light (conductors)
Correctly recorded which materials did not let the bulb light (insulators)

hints: Plastics and paper usually do not.
questions.explanation: This is a practical task. Your teacher will mark it using the rubric.
questions.misconception: All materials let electricity flow.
